subject: physics_2
question_text: The wavelengths of some of the spectral lines obtained in hydrogen spectrum are 1216 Å, 6463 Å and 9549 Å. Which one of these wavelengths belongs to the Paschen series?

mark_split.label: Sort the three wavelengths by region

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. SOURCE DEFECT: the book prints this question TWICE, word for word and with the same answer, as VSAQ 9 (printed p47) and VSAQ 10 (printed p48). It is one question, so it is authored ONCE and carries the FIRST occurrence's reference, vsaq9; the vsaq10 reference is deliberately left out of the unit fragment because merge_p2_units.mjs rejects the same question_id listed twice. The book writes the angstrom as "A°"; it is written Å here. Physics hand-checked with 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹: 1216 Å is Lyman-α (n₂ = 2 → n₁ = 1, ultraviolet); 6463 Å lies in the visible band and belongs to the Balmer series; 9549 Å is infrared and is the n₂ = 8 → n₁ = 3 line of the Paschen series (the Paschen series runs from 18751 Å down to its limit at 8204 Å).

recall_prompt: Say which region each of the three wavelengths falls in, then name the Paschen one.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sort them by region
lines: 1216 Å is ultraviolet — a Lyman line.
6463 Å is in the visible band — a Balmer line.
9549 Å is longer than 7000 Å, so it is
steps.margin_note: First mark. Place all three, not just the answer — that is what shows the reasoning.
steps.why: Each series sits in one region: Lyman is ultraviolet, Balmer is visible, Paschen is infrared. Placing the three wavelengths by region identifies the series at once.
common_mistakes: Calling 6463 Å ultraviolet. The visible band is 4000 Å to 7000 Å.
Placing only the answer and leaving the other two out.

recall.must_convey: That 1216 Å is ultraviolet, 6463 Å is visible and 9549 Å is infrared.
reject: so it belongs to the Paschen series

steps.memory_tip: Three wavelengths, three regions, in order: ultraviolet, visible, infrared.

steps.label: The Paschen line
lines: The Paschen series is emitted when the electron
moves to the third orbit (n₁ = 3), and it lies
So the infrared wavelength is the Paschen line.

lines.text: 9549 Å belongs to the Paschen series

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name n₁ = 3 and give the wavelength.
steps.why: Paschen transitions end on n₁ = 3, where the energy gaps are small, so the photons are low in energy and long in wavelength — the infrared.
common_mistakes: Answering 6463 Å. That is a Balmer line in the visible band.
Writing n₁ = 2 for Paschen. That is Balmer; Paschen ends on n₁ = 3.

recall.must_convey: That 9549 Å is the Paschen line, because Paschen ends on n₁ = 3 and lies in the infrared.
accept: Paschen ends on the third orbit

steps.memory_tip: Paschen ends on 3, small gaps, long waves — the longest of the three given.

insider_note: The book prints this question twice, as VSAQ 9 and again as VSAQ 10 with the same answer — it is one question, and the answer is 9549 Å.
